absent: Allocation search across slots, selection policy and refill or balancing triggers beyond hint validation.
Deallocation coalescing, chunk reclamation, sidelining and to-depopulate transitions beyond empty-page watermarks.
Boot-time first-chunk and reserved-chunk setup, unit mapping construction and read-only finalization order.
Lock ordering against outside locks and interrupt or preemption constraints beyond local spin and mutex use.
Memory accounting and profiling tag lifecycle and NUMA, cache and TLB architectural effects beyond call sites.
Slot failure counting, free-slot maintenance and chunk list migration policies.

findings.text: A block descriptor summarizes occupancy and search state for its slice with a scan hint and start, a longest contiguous run estimate and start, residual free amounts at both edges, earliest free position and total bit count.
Per-object extension optionally associates each object with group accounting state when memory control grouping is enabled and with an allocation tag when allocation profiling is enabled.
A compile-time marker for extension need is defined. Need for the extension holds when allocation profiling is active or when group kernel memory accounting is enabled.

Chunk descriptor aggregates linkage, usage accounting, address and storage references, region maps and hints, population state and optional extension vector. It holds slot list linkage, free byte count, chunk-wide hint block, boundary and allocation bitmaps, cacheline-separated base address, per-block hint array, backing store pointer, immutable and isolated flags, alignment adjustments at both ends, total and populated and empty-populated page counts, optional object extension array and trailing populated bitmap, plus allocation count and largest size when statistics are enabled.
Statistics summary comprises lifetime allocation and deallocation totals, current and peak live allocation counts, current and peak chunk counts and observed minimum and maximum allocation sizes.
Global instances retain cumulative percpu counters and the allocation sizing summary used by reporting.

When statistics are active, recording an area allocation increments lifetime and current counts, raises peak live count if current exceeds it, tightens observed size extremes to include the new size and updates the owning chunk count and largest size. When inactive, recording preserves all state.
When statistics are active, releasing a chunk decrements the global live chunk count with interrupts disabled. When inactive, the operation preserves state without locking.

Successful chunk creation yields a zero-initialized descriptor with page count from unit sizing, allocation and boundary maps sized from region bit count, per-block hints and free bytes equal to full capacity. Any shortage yields no chunk and releases partial resources. Destruction tolerates null and otherwise releases extension, hint, boundary, allocation and descriptor storage.

Internal zeroing allocation requires slab availability and returns null otherwise. Requests of at most one page use zeroed slab storage while larger requests use zeroed virtual storage, and release handles either origin.
Marking a page interval populated sets the corresponding populated range, increases both chunk and global populated totals by the interval length and invokes empty-page accounting update.
In the contiguous-memory backend, population always reports success without work while depopulation and post-unmap flushing perform no action.

A contiguous-backend chunk pairs a fresh descriptor with one contiguous page run whose order derives from the group page count. Every page records its owning chunk, the chunk points at the run and its address and the whole range counts as populated with creation accounting.

Destroying a contiguous-backend chunk records deallocation accounting, clears the owning-chunk link on each page of its run when present, releases the run and frees descriptor storage. A null chunk is ignored.

Addresses within a chunk derive from chunk base plus per-CPU unit offset plus page index scaled by page size. A separate index combines CPU unit number with page position to locate per-CPU page slots. Translating a mapped chunk page is valid only for populated non-immutable chunks.

A single lazily created scratch array sized for all units and pages is reused across populate and depopulate operations. Creation occurs only when a non-zero allocation context is supplied, while the cached accessor never allocates and may return null if never created.

Population backing allocates one page per CPU for each page in the interval with node affinity from the CPU and high memory allowed. Any shortage releases all pages already obtained for the interval and reports out of memory. Release walks the same per-CPU interval and frees only non-null slots.

Mapping installs supplied pages for every CPU over the interval and records the owning chunk on each installed page. Mapping failure unmaps ranges already installed, flushes translation caches and reports failure. Unmapping collects each CPU page via address translation then removes the virtual range per CPU. Cache maintenance surrounds changes with pre-unmap and post-map flushes and translation flush covers the same span after unmapping.

Virtual-backend population succeeds only with scratch space available, per-CPU pages obtained and mappings installed followed by cache flush. Mapping failure releases the pages and reports out of memory. Depopulation requires the scratch cache to exist and then performs flush, unmapping and release. Creation pairs a fresh descriptor with reserved virtual areas and derives base from the first area minus its group offset with creation accounting. Destruction records deallocation, releases areas when present and frees the descriptor, ignoring null.
A block satisfies a request when its recorded longest contiguous run, after rounding its start up to required alignment, still accommodates the requested bit count.
Reporting helpers format labeled integer values, order integers increasingly for sorting and scan all chunk slots to determine the largest per-chunk allocation count.

Global reporting shows allocation sizing, cumulative counters and empty-populated totals, then per-chunk details including allocation counts, size extremes, free and contiguous bytes, first free position and fragmentation summaries derived by walking allocation and boundary maps up to the last allocated bit, classifying runs as allocated or free, sorting extents and extracting live size extremes and free fragment totals and maxima.

Global spin lock serializes internal metadata, statistics, populated counts and chunk slot lists. Area accounting and populated marking require the lock held on entry. Chunk deallocation accounting and statistics display acquire it with interrupts disabled and restore prior state on release.
Allocation mutex serializes chunk creation and destruction, population state changes, mapping extension and the shared scratch page array. The scratch accessor requires this mutex held.
During early initialization a read-only debug filesystem entry named percpu_stats exposes statistics via the display operation.

Chunk progresses from descriptor allocation to backing association to populated and linked for service, then via depopulation and unmapping to backing release and descriptor free. Failure at creation or population returns to no chunk with partial resources released.

Statistics display samples peak allocation count under lock, allocates scratch sized for twice that count plus one outside the lock, then revalidates under lock. If the peak grew meanwhile the buffer is discarded and sampling repeats, otherwise reporting proceeds under lock and releases the buffer afterward.

Undersized reporting buffers, missing scratch cache, page or mapping shortages, descriptor or map allocation failures and absent virtual areas yield out-of-memory or retry rather than partial state. Callers must handle null returns and released partial allocations.

Translating or unmapping warns when applied to immutable chunks or absent mappings, depopulation traps when the required scratch cache is absent and internal allocation warns when slab services are unavailable. These indicate misuse or early-boot ordering violations.
Chunk slot sizing uses base shift five.
Chunk slot failure threshold is three.
Empty populated page watermarks are low two and high four.
Global translation state comprises the percpu base address, the CPU to unit index map and the CPU to unit offset table.
Unit geometry and slot configuration comprise unit page count and byte size, unit count, atom size, slot count, free slot index, sidelined and to-depopulate slot indices and chunk descriptor size.
CPU span extremes and group layout comprise lowest and highest unit CPUs, group count, group offsets and group sizes.
Live chunk references comprise the first chunk, the reserved chunk and the array of chunk slot lists.
Global empty populated page total is visible outside the compilation unit.
Asynchronous balancing enablement is read-mostly state while atomic allocation failure is a plain flag.
Two build-dependent translations convert absolute addresses to percpu pointers. One rebases by the percpu base and start, the other is identity.
Logging prefixes messages with the module name and a compilation marker for trace point creation is defined.
